function.name: calculate_sunrise_and_sunset
function.description: Calculate the sunrise and sunset time of a location for the given date. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location in city, state format.

date.description: The date for which the sunrise and sunset needs to be calculated in yyyy-mm-dd format.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time clock data. If you let me know the current UTC time or your local time, I can calculate what time it would be in New York (taking into account daylight‑saving changes).

But we can't guarantee DST. We could say "I don't have real-time data." But maybe we can use a function? There's no function for current time. So we should respond that we cannot provide real-time. But we can approximate using known timezone: New York is UTC-5 or -4 depending on DST. But we don't know current date. We can ask for clarification. But the user just wants current time. We can respond: "I don't have real-time data." That might be acceptable. Alternatively, we can approximate using the system's time? But we don't have that. So best to say we can't provide real-time.
